record.original_question: How can one classify diagrams in the flat hierarchy obtained by labeling flat crossings by elements of an ordinal and allowing a flat third Reidemeister move in which a line with two labels a slides across a crossing labeled b only when a is greater than b?

evidence.quote: The flat hierarchy is constructed for any ordinal α. We label flat crossings with members of this ordinal. In a flat third Reidemeister move, a line with two a labels can slide across a crossing labeled b only if a is greater than b. This generalizes the usual to theory of flat virtual diagrams to a system with arbitrarily many different types of flat crossings. Classify the diagrams in this hierarchy.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an ordinal $\alpha$. Consider 4-valent planar diagrams (with the usual notion of equivalence by planar isotopy) whose vertices are of two kinds:

(i) "flat crossings" labeled by an element of $\alpha$ (so each non-virtual crossing carries a label $b \in \alpha$ and has no over/under information; the two strands meet transversely);

(ii) "virtual crossings" (drawn as a transverse double point with a small circle).

Generate an equivalence relation on such diagrams by the following local moves:

- The flat (= unsigned) Reidemeister I and II moves applied to flat crossings of any single fixed label.
- The standard virtual Reidemeister moves (the purely virtual R1, R2, R3, and the mixed move that lets a virtual crossing slide past a flat strand).
- A labeled flat third Reidemeister move: a strand carrying two flat crossings each labeled $a \in \alpha$ with another strand may slide across a flat crossing labeled $b \in \alpha$ on that other strand if and only if $a > b$ (in the ordinal order).

Call the resulting equivalence classes the diagrams of the flat hierarchy of height $\alpha$. Provide a classification of these equivalence classes (for example, by producing a complete system of computable invariants, or by exhibiting canonical representatives for each class), for every ordinal $\alpha$.
artifact.status_search_result: Manturov introduced and studied a "flat hierarchy" in Fundamenta Mathematicae, and partial classifications exist for restricted cases (e.g., flat virtual pure tangles). However, no complete classification of diagrams in the full flat hierarchy parameterized by an arbitrary ordinal appears in the literature; the question is generally cited as an unsolved problem in virtual knot theory.

status_evidence.title: Classification of Flat Virtual Pure Tangles
status_evidence.snippet: Flat virtual tangles with no closed components (pure tangles) have been completely classified...
status_evidence.claim: Only restricted subclasses (flat virtual pure tangles) have been fully classified, not the full hierarchy.

status_evidence.title: Virtual knot theory – unsolved problems
status_evidence.snippet: List of unsolved problems in virtual knot theory including questions on flat hierarchy.
status_evidence.claim: The classification problem for the flat hierarchy is listed among unsolved problems.

status_evidence.title: Introduction to Virtual Knot Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses flat virtual knots and hierarchies without giving a complete classification.
status_evidence.claim: No complete classification of the flat hierarchy is provided.
